strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: proposal.apply can recover eligible undeleted items from partial delete_file_transaction evidence under Rust-owned workspace mutation authority.

Delete transaction recovery requires WriteWorkspace permission, current approved unconsumed proposals, fresh preflight, expected target hash matching, source transaction fingerprint validation, applied source item absence, safe path validation, and symlink rejection.
Recovery results record bounded transaction recovery source and per-item delete evidence without raw file content, raw diffs, command output, environment, secrets, or absolute paths.
A headless caller can complete remaining approved deletes from durable partial-failure evidence without shell, git, VSIX policy, or manual deletion.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances controlled_workspace_tools with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: One authorized proposal.apply recovery call can delete one to five eligible undeleted items from partial delete_file_transaction source evidence.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Single-file delete apply lacks source transaction fingerprint validation, unrecovered-source admission, already-deleted source absence revalidation, and recovery status evidence; create/replace recovery does not delete.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless Brownie cannot safely complete partially failed delete transactions under Rust-owned recovery semantics.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M24.1 executes original delete transactions, M23.2 recovers create transactions, and M23.1 executes create transactions; this phase recovers partial delete transaction evidence.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. This extends the existing proposal.apply transaction_recovery_source path.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. This reuses existing apply result, transaction recovery source, recovery status, and transaction item result evidence.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime routes delete transaction recovery, validates source identity/fingerprint/status and applied source absence, deletes eligible remaining targets, verifies post-delete absence, and records bounded recovery evidence.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless automation can recover a partial delete transaction using durable bounded evidence rather than manual deletion or raw ledger scraping.
answers.milestone_progress: This completes the recovery side of M24 controlled deletion and should enable milestone closeout after review and merge.

review_value_gate.review_intent: M24.2 must be reviewed for actual delete_file transaction recovery behavior, source fingerprint and absence revalidation, deny-before-delete safety, expected hash validation, post-delete absence verification, and bounded evidence.

exit_criteria: proposal.apply routes homogeneous delete_file transaction recovery requests to delete recovery instead of replace recovery

Delete recovery requires authorize=true, WriteWorkspace permission, current approved unconsumed proposals, transaction_recovery_source, matching source fingerprint, partial failed delete_file_transaction source status, and no prior successful recovery for that source
Already-applied source delete items must remain absent before any recovery delete occurs

Recovery deletes only eligible failed or not-applied source delete items after expected_target_sha256, empty replacement_content, latest preflight, regular UTF-8 target, protected path denial, parent traversal denial, duplicate or overlap denial, and symlink rejection
No target is deleted when any source or recovery admission precondition fails
Successful recovery records operation=delete_file_transaction_recovery, transaction_recovery_status=Applied, source summary, per-item delete evidence, consumed authorization, and post-delete absence
Ledger and RPC results do not expose raw file content, raw diffs, prompts, provider responses, stdout/stderr, environment, secrets, absolute paths, or canonical paths
Existing single-file delete apply, delete transactions, replace recovery, and create recovery remain compatible
next_phase_candidate_notes: After M24.2 merges, close out M24 unless autonomous review identifies a distinct non-wrapper controlled deletion runtime capability gap.
